image_description: A high-angle, close-up shot of a Nile crocodile resting on a concrete or stone bank next to water. The view focuses primarily on the dorsal side of the crocodile, showing its tail, hindquarters, and part of its back. The head is partially visible at the top right, but the snout tip and eyes are largely out of frame or obscured by the angle. The skin texture is highly detailed, showing distinct osteoderms (scutes).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is positioned at the very edge of the frame and angled away; the full triangular shape and snout profile are not fully visible to verify the V-shape vs U-shape distinction.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and the jawline is mostly occluded by the angle and framing; individual teeth interlocking cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eyes are either out of frame or too far in the background/obscured by the angle to see pupil shape or membranes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tip of the snout is outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body clearly shows an elongated structure covered in heavy, bony armor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct, raised osteoderms are clearly visible running in parallel rows down the spine and tail.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration matches (dark ridges, lighter yellowish/tan valleys) and the texture appears rough and calcified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a dorsal/top-down view; the belly (ventral side) is completely occluded against the ground.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only a small portion of one hind limb is visible at the very edge; digits and webbing are not clear enough to count or verify structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is prominently featured, showing significant musculature and lateral compression typical of crocodilians.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The very end of the tail tip appears slightly 'mushy' or melted into the background rock/water interface. The distinct scute pattern dissolves into a blur rather than ending in a sharp, natural point.

artifact_observations.location: Right hind limb area (top right edge)
artifact_observations.reasoning: The transition from the body to the hind leg is indistinct. The leg seems to merge with the body mass without a clear joint definition, and the foot structure is ambiguous/blob-like.
The reflection and refraction of the crocodile's body in the water are inconsistent. The submerged parts do not align perfectly with the above-water parts, suggesting slight geometric warping.

To assess overall texture consistency and detect subtle melting artifacts in the high-frequency details of the skin.
To verify the physical plausibility of the crocodile's position relative to the water and bank, checking for floating or sinking errors.
